Bar heights from left to right: Apr (~29,500), Jan (~40,000, tallest), Jun (~17,500), Feb (~20,000), Mar (~27,000), May (near baseline, smallest).

public_definitions: User goal: Review the monthly water pumping dashboard and decide whether May should be handled as a standard low-pumping follow-up or escalated as a critical low-pumping anomaly for this reporting cycle.
Primary field label: May low-pumping route
Option 1: Route May to standard low-pumping follow-up
Option 2: Escalate May to critical low-pumping anomaly review
Option 3: Send May to background monthly record filing
Routing criterion (readonly): May low-pumping severity route
Review scope (readonly): May low-pumping severity review
uncertain: No explicit numeric threshold or policy table on the page defines the boundary between 'standard low-pumping follow-up' and 'critical low-pumping anomaly'; the routing decision must be inferred from May's relative position as the lowest bar.
The exact m3 value for May is not printed; it is only visually below the 10,000 tick, so its precise magnitude is an estimate.
The x-axis month order (Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, May) is non-chronological; this is taken literally as displayed and not reordered.
